<!-- ===== docs/getting-started.md ===== -->

# Getting started

## Requirements

| Need | Why |
|---|---|
| Node.js ≥ 18 | runtime (tested on 20 / 22) |
| `ffmpeg` on PATH | file/URL container decode, mixed recording, muxing and RTMP encoding |
| `ffprobe` on PATH | video metadata and folder recording validation |
| `yt-dlp` on PATH | only for `joinYouTube()` / `resolveYouTube()` |
| A **user** account session | Telegram does not allow bots to join voice chats |
| `api_id` / `api_hash` | from <https://my.telegram.org> |

Install ffmpeg:

```bash
sudo apt-get install ffmpeg        # Debian/Ubuntu
brew install ffmpeg yt-dlp         # macOS
```

## Install the package

```bash
npm install --allow-git=all github:kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js#v0.8.0
```

npm 12+ blocks git dependencies by default (`EALLOWGIT`); `--allow-git=all`
opts in for this install.

`ntgcalls` provides prebuilt native binaries (Linux x64/arm64, macOS arm64,
Windows x64). If your npm version skips the platform binary when installing from
a git URL, install it manually — see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md).

## Get a user session

You need a logged-in **user** client. Two common paths:

### teleproto / GramJS (StringSession)

```js
import { TelegramClient } from 'teleproto';
import { StringSession } from 'teleproto/sessions/index.js';

const client = new TelegramClient(new StringSession(''), API_ID, API_HASH, {});
await client.start({
  phoneNumber: async () => '+62…',
  phoneCode:   async () => /* code from the Telegram app */,
  password:    async () => /* 2FA password if enabled */,
});
const sessionString = client.session.save(); // store this securely, reuse later
```

Reuse it next time with `new StringSession(sessionString)` + `await client.connect()`.

### mtcute

```js
import { TelegramClient } from '@mtcute/node';
const client = new TelegramClient({ apiId: API_ID, apiHash: API_HASH, storage: 'account.session' });
await client.start({ phone: () => '+62…', code: () => /* … */, password: () => /* … */ });
```

> Keep session strings and 2FA passwords secret (e.g. a `chmod 600` file or a
> secrets manager). Never commit them.

## First stream

```js
import { TgCallsClient } from 'tgcalls-js';

const tg = new TgCallsClient({ client });

tg.on('connectionChange', (chatId, state) => console.log('state:', state));
tg.on('streamEnd', ({ chatId }) => console.log('track finished in', chatId));

// chat accepts a marked id (-100…), @username, or t.me link
await tg.join(-1001234567890, { kind: 'file', path: './song.mp3' });
```

The call auto-leaves when the track ends (`autoLeave` defaults to `true`). To keep
the call open and queue more tracks, set `autoLeave: false` and use `setSource()`
inside `streamEnd`.

## Verify your setup (no credentials)

```bash
npm test     # offline suite: fake MTProto + real ntgcalls core
npm run smoke
```

Next: the [Guide](guide.md) for video, presentation, idle, and adapters, or the
[API reference](api.md).


<!-- ===== docs/guide.md ===== -->

# Guide

## The join flow

Every join follows the same ordered sequence (do not reorder it):

1. `channels.getFullChannel` (or `messages.getFullChat` for basic groups) → `fullChat.call` (InputGroupCall).
2. `ntgcalls.createCall(chatId)` → native join params JSON (contains the **ssrc**).
3. `ntgcalls.setStreamSources(chatId, CAPTURE, …)` — set media **before** the MTProto join so it flows immediately.
4. `phone.joinGroupCall(params)` → wait for `UpdateGroupCallConnection`.
5. `ntgcalls.connect(chatId, connParams)` → media starts.

The same join-params string is sent in `JoinGroupCall`, and its ssrc is reused for
`LeaveGroupCall`. The library handles all of this; you only call `join()`.

## Sources

`AudioSource` is one of:

```ts
{ kind: 'file'; path: string }                 // any ffmpeg-readable file
{ kind: 'url'; url: string; audioUrl?: string } // direct media URL; audioUrl for split video/audio
{ kind: 'shell'; command: string }              // command piping s16le 48kHz stereo PCM to stdout
```

- **file / url** are decoded by ffmpeg to PCM (`-f s16le -ac 2 -ar 48000 pipe:1`).
- **shell** gives you full control; the command must output raw PCM at 48 kHz stereo.
- `joinYouTube()` resolves a page URL to a direct media URL via yt-dlp, then joins.
  With video it requests separate `bestvideo + bestaudio` streams (`audioUrl` carries the audio).

## Video

Pass `video` to `join()` to stream video from the same file/URL:

```js
await tg.join(chatId, { kind: 'file', path: './clip.mp4' }, {
  video: { width: 854, height: 480, fps: 30 },
});
```

- Dimensions are probed and kept **even** (YUV420p requirement); scaling is proportional.
- `video: false` disables video; omitting it streams audio only.
- Start at 854×480@30 on small VPS; raise to 720p60 / 1080p60 if the host keeps up
  (verified stable on a 4-vCPU cloud VM).
- For YouTube video, prefer `vp9`/`avc1` over AV1 (AV1 is too heavy to decode in real time).

### Camera vs presentation

- `video` alone → **camera** channel.
- `presentation: true` (or `startPresentation()`) → **screen-share** channel.
- Camera and screen **cannot be active at the same time** in one call; starting a
  presentation replaces the camera channel.

```js
await tg.startPresentation(chatId, { kind: 'file', path: './slides.mp4' }, { width: 1280, height: 720 });
await tg.stopPresentation(chatId); // call stays, camera can resume
```

> `setStreamSources` **replaces** all devices: any device omitted from a description
> is dropped. The library rebuilds the video channel on `setSource()` so video is not
> silently lost when you swap audio.

## Idle presence

`joinIdle()` joins with no media — useful for a bot that waits in a voice chat:

```js
await tg.joinIdle(chatId, { autoLeave: false });
```

- On UDP-capable hosts this is stable indefinitely (verified: **40+ minutes**, no disconnect).
- On UDP-blocked hosts, a regular RTC join gets ICE-timeout-kicked after ~25s. With
  `allowCreate: true`, `joinIdle()` creates a missing call in **RTMP-stream** mode and
  joins muted; an existing call is not converted.

## Queue / swapping tracks

Built-in playlist (v0.4.0): queue tracks and they advance automatically when each
one ends — no manual `streamEnd` wiring needed.

```js
const tg = new TgCallsClient({ client });
await tg.play(chatId, first);          // join + start now
await tg.enqueue(chatId, second);      // play after first
await tg.then(chatId, third);          // alias of enqueue
await tg.playOnHold(chatId, holdLoop); // looped while the queue is empty

// later, from a command handler:
await tg.skip(chatId);                 // jump to the next track
tg.getCurrent(chatId);                 // the playing source
tg.getQueue(chatId);                   // queued sources (copy)
await tg.clearQueue(chatId);           // empty queue + hold
```

The call stays open while tracks are queued; it only auto-leaves when the queue
**and** hold are empty. `skip()` with nothing queued pauses playback (call stays).

For manual control, `setSource()` swaps the audio without leaving and keeps the
video channel intact:

```js
tg.on('streamEnd', async ({ chatId }) => {
  const next = queue.shift();
  if (next) await tg.setSource(chatId, next);
});
await tg.join(chatId, first, { autoLeave: false });
```

With `autoLeave: true` and **no** `streamEnd` handler (and no playlist), the call
auto-leaves when the stream ends.

## Recording

Record incoming call audio (what other participants say) to a file:

```js
await tg.join(chatId, music, { autoLeave: false });
await tg.startRecording(chatId, './call.wav');        // or .mp3 / .opus
// ... later
const path = await tg.stopRecording(chatId);          // finalizes the file
tg.isRecording(chatId);                               // false now
```

ntgcalls mixes all remote speakers natively and pipes PCM to ffmpeg, which encodes
to the path (container from the extension). Options: `{ sampleRate: 48000, channels: 1 }`.
One recording per chat; starting again replaces it. Leaving the call stops it too.
After `stopRecording`, give ffmpeg a moment to finalize before reading the file.

## P2P calls (incoming)

> **✅ Verified live** (0.7.0): the call reaches ICE `CONNECTED` and audio is heard
> by the caller. Requires a GramJS/teleproto client.

Answer incoming 1-on-1 voice calls and stream audio into them (e.g. a voice bot):

```js
await tg.listenCalls({
  source: { kind: 'file', path: './song.mp3' },
  onIncoming: ({ userId }) => { console.log('call from', userId); return true; },
});
// ... later
await tg.stopListeningCalls();
```

The DH key exchange and WebRTC engine run in ntgcalls; tgcalls-js orchestrates the
MTProto signaling (`phone.acceptCall`, signaling relay, teardown on hangup).
Requires a GramJS/teleproto or mtcute client. `autoAccept` defaults to true; `onIncoming` can
reject specific callers. `callUser()` places outgoing calls after `listenCalls()` is configured.
The roadmap branch also exposes an experimental native conference core with explicit
security limits; see [Roadmap APIs](roadmap-api.md).

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `streamEnd` | `{ chatId, source, willAutoLeave }` | fires once per playback; with video, waits for both audio and video to end |
| `connectionChange` | `(chatId, state)` | `state` is a numeric `ConnectionState` (see below) |
| `update` | raw TL update | pass-through of group-call-related updates |

`ConnectionState` (numeric enum from ntgcalls):

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | CONNECTING |
| 2 | CONNECTED |
| 4 | FAILED |
| 8 | TIMEOUT |
| 16 | CLOSED |

A handler that throws/rejects is logged (via the `logger` option) and never crashes
the process. Multiple handlers per event all run (registration order); `on`/`once`
return an unsubscribe function and `off` removes one. Registering any `streamEnd`
handler suppresses auto-leave.

## Adapters / client detection

`TgCallsClient` auto-detects the client:

- **mtcute** — has `.call` + `.onRawUpdate.add` → `MtcuteAdapter`.
- **GramJS / teleproto** — has `.invoke` → `GramjsAdapter`.
- **custom** — pass an object implementing `MTProtoAdapter` (`isAdapter: true`).

```js
import { GramjsAdapter, MtcuteAdapter, createAdapter } from 'tgcalls-js';
const adapter = createAdapter(client, { Api }); // or new GramjsAdapter(client, { Api })
const tg = new TgCallsClient({ client: adapter });
```

When mixing `telegram` and `teleproto` in one process, pass the matching `Api`
namespace per client to avoid ambiguous TL auto-detection. mtcute needs no `Api`.

> mtcute TL `Long` objects (low/high) are preserved **by reference** — do not convert
> them to JS bigint. GramJS/teleproto use plain bigint.

## Lifecycle & cleanup

- `leave(chat)` stops the native call and sends `LeaveGroupCall` (best-effort both).
- A failed `join()` cleans up the native call and leaves any zombie participant.
- On native `CLOSED`/`FAILED`, the library leaves via MTProto **before** notifying
  listeners, so you can safely destroy the MTProto client from the callback.
- `await tg.dispose()` before disposing the MTProto client; avoid `process.exit()`
  immediately after native use (WebRTC teardown can abort).

## Typed errors

```js
import { AlreadyInCallError, NoVoiceChatError, TgCallsError } from 'tgcalls-js';
try {
  await tg.join(chatId, src);
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof AlreadyInCallError) console.log('busy in', e.chatId);
  else if (e instanceof NoVoiceChatError) console.log('start a voice chat first');
}
```

All library errors extend `TgCallsError` (which extends `Error`). See the
[API reference](api.md#errors).


<!-- ===== docs/api.md ===== -->

# API reference

All exports come from the package root (`import … from 'tgcalls-js'`).

New APIs on the unreleased roadmap branch are documented in [Roadmap APIs](roadmap-api.md). They are not included in the `v0.8.0` tag.

## `TgCallsClient`

### Constructor

```ts
new TgCallsClient(options: TgCallsOptions)
```

#### `TgCallsOptions`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `client` | `MTProtoLike \| MtcuteLike \| MTProtoAdapter` | — | teleproto/GramJS client, mtcute client, or a custom adapter |
| `Api` | `unknown` | auto | TL API namespace; pass per client when mixing `telegram` + `teleproto` |
| `ffmpegPath` | `string` | `"ffmpeg"` | ffmpeg binary |
| `ffprobePath` | `string` | `"ffprobe"` | ffprobe binary |
| `ytDlpPath` | `string` | `"yt-dlp"` | yt-dlp binary |
| `logger` | `{ error(...args: unknown[]): void }` | `console.error` | sink for internal warnings (e.g. a throwing event handler) |

### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ntg` | `NTgCalls` | the underlying native instance (advanced use) |

### Methods

#### Joining

```ts
join(chat: ChatRef, source: AudioSource, options?: JoinOptions): Promise<JoinResult>
joinYouTube(chat: ChatRef, url: string, options?: JoinOptions): Promise<JoinResult>
joinIdle(chat: ChatRef, options?: JoinOptions): Promise<JoinResult>
resolveYouTube(url: string, video?: boolean): Promise<string | null>
```

- `join` — join the voice chat and stream `source`. Throws `AlreadyInCallError` if
  already in a call (or mid-join) in that chat.
- `joinYouTube` — resolve `url` via yt-dlp, then `join`.
- `joinIdle` — join with no media. With `allowCreate: true`, creates a missing call
  in RTMP-stream mode (for UDP-blocked hosts); an existing call is not converted.
  Throws `NoVoiceChatError` if there is no call and `allowCreate` is not set.
- `resolveYouTube` — resolve a page URL to a direct media URL (or `null`).

#### Presentation (screen share)

```ts
startPresentation(chat: ChatRef, source: Exclude<AudioSource, {kind:'shell'}>, video?: VideoOptions): Promise<void>
stopPresentation(chat: ChatRef): Promise<void>
```

`startPresentation` joins the presentation channel with a file/url video source
(replaces the camera channel). `stopPresentation` leaves the presentation channel;
the call stays.

#### Playback control

```ts
setSource(chat: ChatRef, source: AudioSource): Promise<void>  // swap audio, keep video (queue)
pause(chat: ChatRef): Promise<boolean>
resume(chat: ChatRef): Promise<boolean>
mute(chat: ChatRef): Promise<boolean>
unmute(chat: ChatRef): Promise<boolean>
time(chat: ChatRef): Promise<number>                          // seconds streamed
```

#### Playlist / queue

```ts
play(chat: ChatRef, source: AudioSource, options?: JoinOptions): Promise<JoinResult>
enqueue(chat: ChatRef, source: AudioSource): Promise<void>   // alias: then()
then(chat: ChatRef, source: AudioSource): Promise<void>
skip(chat: ChatRef): Promise<void>
playOnHold(chat: ChatRef, source: AudioSource | null): Promise<void>
clearQueue(chat: ChatRef): Promise<void>
getCurrent(chat: ChatRef): AudioSource | null                // sync
getQueue(chat: ChatRef): AudioSource[]                       // sync; copy
```

- `play` — join (if not already in a call) and start `source` now, replacing the
  current track. The call is kept open (`autoLeave` off) so the playlist decides
  when to leave.
- `enqueue` / `then` — queue a track after the current one. Joins if no call is
  active; starts immediately if the call is idle; otherwise appends to the queue.
- `skip` — jump to the next queued track (or the hold track). With nothing queued,
  pauses playback (the call stays open).
- `playOnHold` — set a track looped while the queue is empty (hold music); `null` clears it.
- `clearQueue` — empty the queue and clear the hold track (current track keeps playing).
- `getCurrent` / `getQueue` — inspect the playing track and queued tracks (sync;
  numeric id or previously-resolved alias).

When a track ends, the next queued track (or the hold loop) starts automatically.
The call only auto-leaves when the queue **and** hold are empty (and `autoLeave` is
on with no `streamEnd` handler). The lower-level `setSource()` still works for
manual swapping.

#### Recording

```ts
startRecording(chat: ChatRef, path: string, options?: RecordOptions): Promise<RecordingInfo>
stopRecording(chat: ChatRef): Promise<string | null>   // returns the recorded path
getRecording(chat: ChatRef): RecordingInfo | null      // sync
isRecording(chat: ChatRef): boolean                    // sync
```

Records **incoming** call audio (what other participants say). ntgcalls mixes all
remote speakers natively and pipes s16le PCM to ffmpeg, which encodes to `path` —
the container is inferred from the extension (`.wav`, `.mp3`, `.opus`, …).
`RecordOptions`: `sampleRate` (default 48000), `channels` (default 1 mono).

Requires an active call. One recording per chat; calling `startRecording` again
replaces it. For a string target, `stopRecording` closes the native mixed-audio writer; this legacy path does not attest encoder success. Folder recording uses owned writers and validation before reporting `saved`. Leaving the call also stops recording; see [folder recording](roadmap-api.md#participant-folder-recording).

#### P2P calls (incoming)

> **✅ Verified live** (tgcalls-js 0.7.0): incoming 1-on-1 calls connect and stream
> audio end-to-end (ICE `CONNECTED`, RTP flowing, audio heard by the caller).
>
> Notes for implementers:
> - Byte parameters passed to the ntgcalls binding must be **plain JS arrays**
>   (`Array.from(buf)`); `Buffer`/`Uint8Array` throw `An array was expected`.
>   The wrapper does this for you.
> - Signaling must use **V2 external signaling** (`8.0.0`/`9.0.0`). Passing
>   `12.0.0`/`13.0.0` makes ntgcalls route signaling over an SCTP data channel and
>   the call times out. `listenCalls` restricts the version list automatically.
> - Set `debug: true` to log per-step signaling/ICE diagnostics.

```ts
listenCalls(options: ListenCallsOptions): Promise<void>
stopListeningCalls(): Promise<void>
activeCallPeers(): bigint[]
```

`listenCalls` answers incoming 1-on-1 voice calls and streams `options.source` into
them. `ListenCallsOptions`: `source` (AudioSource), `autoAccept` (default true),
`onIncoming({userId, callId}) => boolean` (gate to accept/reject), `ffmpegPath`,
`debug` (verbose `[p2p]` signaling/ICE logs, default false), `logger`. The DH exchange + WebRTC run in ntgcalls; the library handles the MTProto
signaling. Requires a GramJS/teleproto or mtcute client. One listener per client; calling
again replaces it. `stopListeningCalls` hangs up active calls.

> **mtcute:** call `client.start()`, not `client.connect()` — the updates loop
> (and therefore every `updatePhoneCall`) only runs after `start()`.

#### Outgoing calls

```ts
callUser(userId: ChatRef, options?: OutgoingCallOptions): Promise<bigint>
```

Calls `userId` and streams the same `source` into the call once the callee answers.
Requires `listenCalls()` first — that installs the update handler which drives the
accept → confirm steps. Returns the Telegram call id. The call is hung up by
`stopListeningCalls()` / `dispose()`, or when the peer ends it.

```ts
await tgcalls.listenCalls({ source: { kind: 'file', path: 'song.mp3' }, video: { width: 640, height: 360, fps: 25 } });
const callId = await tgcalls.callUser(123456789n, { video: true });
```

How it works: `initExchange` is called with a `null` gaHash so the native core
returns `SHA256(g_a)` for `phone.requestCall`; on `PhoneCallAccepted` the library
calls `exchangeKeys(gB, 0)` (the native core computes the fingerprint) and then
`phone.confirmCall(gA, keyFingerprint)`. `phone.requestCall` returns
`USER_PRIVACY_RESTRICTED` when the callee only accepts calls from contacts.

An experimental native conference core is available on this branch. Full security conformance, removal/rekey and encrypted in-call messages remain blocked on native 3.0.7; see [Roadmap APIs](roadmap-api.md#experimental-conference-core).

#### Lifecycle

```ts
leave(chat: ChatRef): Promise<void>   // ntgcalls.stop + phone.leaveGroupCall (best-effort)
dispose(options?: { preserveState?: boolean }): Promise<void> // stop owned calls/publishers; preserve desired state for planned restart
```

#### Introspection

```ts
activeCalls(): bigint[]                       // marked ids of all active calls
getCall(chat: ChatRef): ActiveCall | null     // sync; numeric id or previously-resolved alias
isActive(chat: ChatRef): boolean              // sync; same alias rules
resolveChatId(chat: ChatRef): Promise<bigint> // username / t.me link / id → marked id
getEmojiFingerprint(chat: ChatRef | ConferenceHandle): Promise<string | null>  // 4 emojis, null when not in that call
getConnectionMode(chat: ChatRef): Promise<string | null>    // NONE | RTC | STREAM | RTMP
```

`getEmojiFingerprint` returns the four-emoji key check both sides must compare out
of band (a mismatch means a man in the middle). `getConnectionMode` reports how the
native core carries the media: direct `RTC`, a Telegram `STREAM`, or `RTMP`.

#### Events

```ts
on<K extends keyof TgCallsEvents>(event: K, handler: TgCallsEvents[K]): () => void
off<K extends keyof TgCallsEvents>(event: K, handler: TgCallsEvents[K]): void
once<K extends keyof TgCallsEvents>(event: K, handler: TgCallsEvents[K]): () => void
```

Multiple handlers per event are supported — all run in registration order. `on`
and `once` return an unsubscribe function; `off` removes a specific handler.
`once` runs a handler a single time then removes it. A handler that throws/rejects
is logged (via `logger`) and never blocks the other handlers or crashes the process.
Registering any `streamEnd` handler suppresses auto-leave.

`remoteSourceChange(chatId, { ssrc, state, device, peer?, endpoint?, origin? })` reports native P2P source notifications and attributed MTProto participant transitions for active group registries. Group discovery uses MTProto updates because the inspected native binary does not emit group participant discovery. Removed sources map to `StreamStatus.IDLING`. Folder recording manages segment creation automatically.

## Types

### `ChatRef`

```ts
type ChatRef = string | number | bigint;
```

Async methods accept a marked id (`-100…`), `@username`, or `t.me` link. Sync
`getCall()` / `isActive()` accept numeric ids or aliases previously resolved by this
client. `activeCalls()` always returns marked ids.

### `AudioSource`

```ts
type AudioSource =
  | { kind: 'file'; path: string }
  | { kind: 'url'; url: string; audioUrl?: string }
  | { kind: 'shell'; command: string };
```

### `JoinOptions`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `muted` | `boolean` | `false` | join with microphone muted |
| `autoLeave` | `boolean` | `true` | leave when the audio stream ends (suppressed by a `streamEnd` handler) |
| `allowCreate` | `boolean` | `false` | create a missing voice chat (requires admin rights) |
| `inviteHash` | `string` | — | invite hash when joining via a call invite link |
| `video` | `VideoOptions \| false` | — | share video from the same source |
| `presentation` | `boolean` | `false` | use the presentation channel for this call |

### `VideoOptions`

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `width` | `number` | probed / 640 |
| `height` | `number` | probed / 360 |
| `fps` | `number` | probed / 25 |
| `adjustByHeight` | `boolean` | `true` |

### `VideoQuality` (presets)

```ts
VideoQuality.UHD_4K   // { width: 3840, height: 2160, fps: 60 }
VideoQuality.QHD_2K   // { width: 2560, height: 1440, fps: 60 }
VideoQuality.FHD_1080p// { width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 60 }
VideoQuality.HD_720p  // { width: 1280, height: 720,  fps: 30 }
VideoQuality.SD_480p  // { width: 854,  height: 480,  fps: 30 }
VideoQuality.SD_360p  // { width: 640,  height: 360,  fps: 30 }
```

### `JoinResult`

```ts
interface JoinResult { chatId: bigint; call: unknown; ssrc: number; }
```

### `ActiveCall`

```ts
interface ActiveCall {
  chatId: bigint; call: unknown; ssrc: number; source: AudioSource;
  videoActive: boolean; presentationActive: boolean;
  muted: boolean; autoLeave: boolean; joinedAt: number;
}
```

### `StreamEndInfo`

```ts
interface StreamEndInfo {
  chatId: bigint;
  source: AudioSource | null;
  willAutoLeave: boolean; // true when no streamEnd handler is registered and autoLeave is on
}
```

### `TgCallsEvents`

```ts
interface TgCallsEvents {
  streamEnd: (info: StreamEndInfo) => void | Promise<void>;
  connectionChange: (chatId: bigint, state: ConnectionState) => void | Promise<void>;
  update: (update: unknown) => void | Promise<void>;
}
```

`ConnectionState` is a numeric enum (from ntgcalls): `CONNECTING=1`, `CONNECTED=2`,
`FAILED=4`, `TIMEOUT=8`, `CLOSED=16`.

## Errors

All extend `TgCallsError` (which extends `Error`); `error.name` is the class name.

| Class | Extra | Thrown when |
|---|---|---|
| `TgCallsError` | — | base class for all library errors |
| `AlreadyInCallError` | `chatId: bigint` | `join`/`joinIdle` while already in a call (or mid-join) in that chat |
| `NoVoiceChatError` | — | no active voice chat and `allowCreate` not set |
| `UnrecognizedClientError` | — | the `client` is neither GramJS-family, mtcute, nor an adapter |

## Adapters

```ts
class GramjsAdapter implements MTProtoAdapter { constructor(client: MTProtoLike, opts?: { Api?: unknown }) }
class MtcuteAdapter implements MTProtoAdapter { constructor(client: MtcuteLike) }
function createAdapter(client: SupportedClient, opts?: { Api?: unknown }): MTProtoAdapter
function isAdapter(client: unknown): client is MTProtoAdapter
function isMtcuteClient(client: unknown): client is MtcuteLike
function isGramjsClient(client: unknown): client is MTProtoLike
```

`MTProtoAdapter` interface: `resolveChatId`, `getGroupCall`, `joinGroupCall`,
`leaveGroupCall`, `joinPresentationCall`, `leavePresentationCall`,
`extractConnectionParams`, `installUpdateHandler`, optional `dispose`.

## Media helpers

```ts
pcmCommand(source: AudioSource, opts: TgCallsOptions): string
audioDescription(source: AudioSource, opts: TgCallsOptions): object
videoDescription(source, video: VideoOptions, opts): object
probeVideo(filePathOrUrl: string, opts, target?: VideoOptions): Promise<{width,height,fps}>
resolveYouTube(url: string, opts, video?: boolean): Promise<string | null>
resolveYouTubeStreams(url: string, opts, maxHeight?: number): Promise<{ url: string; audioUrl?: string } | null>
```

## TL helpers

```ts
loadTl(provided?: unknown): AnyApi   // resolve/cache the raw TL namespace (telegram → teleproto)
resetTlCache(): void
loadEvents(...): unknown
```


<!-- ===== docs/roadmap-api.md ===== -->

# Roadmap APIs (unreleased)

These APIs are available on the roadmap branch and are not part of the `v0.8.0` tag. Read [the roadmap](ROADMAP.md) for fixture evidence, live gates and native blockers.

## P2P preflight and recording

```ts
const reason = await tg.getCallDenialReason(peer, { video: true });
const allowed = await tg.canRequestCall(peer, { video: true });
// No ringing RPC is made by either preflight call.
await tg.listenCalls({ source: { kind: 'file', path: './tone.mp3' } });
await tg.callUser(peer, {
  video: true,
  record: { path: './remote.mp4', video: true },
});
```

A preflight uses the latest profile/session flags and can become stale before dialing. Denial reasons include invalid/self/bot/deleted peers, missing user session, blocking/privacy restrictions, and unavailable audio/video calls. Unknown network failures reject. `callUser` still needs `listenCalls` so update/signaling handlers are running.

`OutgoingCallOptions.record` inherits the listener default when omitted, disables it with `false`, or replaces it with a path/`CallRecordOptions`. Concurrent calls cannot use the same active target. P2P recording captures the remote media, not a mix with the local source.

## Participant folder recording

```ts
await tg.joinIdle(group);
tg.on('recordingStopped', (chatId, info) => {
  // info: path, peer?, device, segment, reason, status, error?
  // Only status === 'saved' means a closed and validated folder artifact.
});
tg.on('recordingError', (chatId, error) => console.error(error));
await tg.startRecording(group, { dir: './recordings', video: true });
const folder = await tg.stopRecording(group);
```

`FolderRecordingTarget` accepts `dir`, `video`, `sampleRate` (default 48000), and `channels` (1 or 2, default 1). Each peer kind/id, device, endpoint and resolution change receives a new segment. Microphone output is WAV; camera/screen output is H.264/AAC MP4. A manifest records identity, SSRC, segment timing, dropped frames and finalization status.

The recorder obtains all participant pages and follows MTProto deltas. `remoteSourceChange` retains native enum fields `ssrc`, `device`, `state` and adds optional `peer`, `endpoint`, `origin`. Group updates use `origin:'mtproto'`; a removed source maps to `StreamStatus.IDLING`. Native P2P source notifications do not identify group participants.

Only one PLAYBACK recording sink owns a group at a time. Starting another recording stops the previous one. Unified RTMP viewer media cannot be attributed per participant and is rejected for folder recording. Mixed audio recording with a string path remains available separately.

Folder `stopRecording` and group `leave` drain accepted frames, close writers, probe files and emit results before returning. Disk/encoder/probe failures remain observable; failed recovery sources are retained. Camera/screen uses a local monotonic arrival timeline with CFR output; native audio and video timestamp fields are not assumed to share a clock. Live AV-sync acceptance is still open.

## RTMP publication and stream viewing

```ts
// Fetching does not revoke the existing key. Never log this result.
const endpoint = await tg.getStreamRtmpUrl(group);
const publisher = await tg.joinRtmp(group, endpoint.url, endpoint.key);
await publisher.play({ kind: 'file', path: './clip.mp4' }, { width: 640, height: 360, fps: 25 });
publisher.queue({ kind: 'file', path: './next.mp4' });
publisher.hold({ kind: 'file', path: './hold.mp4' });
await publisher.skip();
await publisher.stop();

const viewer = await secondClient.joinStreamMode(group);
// viewer.mode: 'RTMP' | 'STREAM'; server chooses the actual transport.
await secondClient.leave(group);
```

`joinRtmp(chat,url,key,options)` prepares a publisher. It starts encoding only when `play()` is called, or when `options.source` is supplied. Existing ordinary voice chats are refused. `allowCreate:true` permits creation of a missing RTMP call, not conversion of an active RTC call. Files and URLs are accepted; caller-owned raw PCM shell sources are refused for RTMP.

The publisher uses ffmpeg H.264/AAC in FLV. State is `ready`, `starting`, `publishing`, `reconnecting`, `paused`, `stopped` or `failed`. Readiness requires encoder progress. `reconnect:{maxAttempts,maxDelayMs,baseDelayMs?}` bounds retries and restarts the current source from its beginning. POSIX pause/resume suspends/resumes the process; a long pause may expire the server connection. `close()` permanently closes the publisher. `dispose()` closes owned publishers.

`joinStreamMode(chat,{requireStream:true})` joins muted with the original native payload, downloads segments from the exact media DC and supplies replies to the native decoder. If the server selects RTC it rolls back and rejects. Set `requireStream:false` to explicitly allow RTC. There is no invented MTProto flag that forces STREAM mode. `broadcastError` reports failed downloads/recovery. Native broadcast download callbacks are separate from RTMP uploading.

## Experimental conference core

```ts
const handle = await tg.createConference({ source: { kind: 'file', path: './tone.mp3' } });
const link = await tg.exportConferenceInvite(handle);
const other = await secondClient.joinConference({ slug: 'invite_slug' });
await tg.inviteConferenceParticipants(handle, [peer], { video: false }); // rings peer
const emojiDisplay = await tg.getEmojiFingerprint(handle);
const capabilities = tg.getConferenceCapabilities();
await tg.leaveConference(handle);
```

`ConferenceRef` is `{slug}`, `{inviteMessageId}` or `{id,accessHash}`. `ConferenceHandle` is distinct from a group `ChatRef`; its native ID follows a fresh generation on recovery. Options include source, video, muted, videoStopped and cancellation signal. Capture is installed after native conference initialization. Private native keys and signed blocks are never synthesized by the wrapper.

`activeConferences()` lists active handles. `conferenceError` reports asynchronous chain/poll failures. `getEmojiFingerprint(handle)` returns a native display value or null while pending; it is not an attestation of chain health or current cryptographic conformance.

On `ntgcalls@3.0.7`, `removeConferenceParticipants`, `rekeyConference`, and `sendConferenceMessage` reject `UnsupportedNativeCapabilityError`. Encrypted application decoding and crypto-health are also unavailable. The wrapper has no plaintext or JavaScript crypto fallback. `getConferenceCapabilities()` reports these limits and `fullSecurityConformance:false`, `liveVerified:false`. Two-account Telegram audio/video and emoji validation remain open.

## Explicit restart recovery

```ts
const tg = new TgCallsClient({ client, statePath: './private/calls.json' });
await tg.play(group, { kind: 'file', path: './song.mp3' }, { autoLeave: false });
await tg.enqueue(group, { kind: 'file', path: './next.mp3' });
await tg.flushState();
await tg.dispose({ preserveState: true });

// New authorized MTProto client with its own running updates loop:
const restarted = new TgCallsClient({ client: nextClient, statePath: './private/calls.json' });
const { restored, skipped, failed } = await restarted.resumeFromState();
```

Construction never rejoins. The private versioned file stores desired group chats, current source, queue/hold, mute/pause, video settings and recording targets. Writes use private temporary files, fsync, atomic rename and conflict detection. Unknown schema versions are refused without overwriting the file. `persistenceError` makes errors observable.

Restore refetches current group calls, uses fresh native SSRCs, mutes/pauses capture before connecting, restores the queue, and opens recording in a fresh segment/directory. It starts media from the beginning. `restore.resolveSource` can refresh expiring URLs. Persisting shell sources requires `persistence.allowShell:true`; replaying them separately requires `restore.allowShell:true`. The default skips shell groups.

`dispose()` normally removes groups explicitly left; use `preserveState:true` for a planned restart. P2P sessions, conference private keys, native sockets and RTMP keys are not persisted or automatically redialed. `resumeFromState` returns per-chat results and does not create a missing group call by default.

## Real-time external frame bridge (Voice AI / live PCM)

```ts
await tg.join(group, { kind: 'external', sampleRate: 48000, channels: 1 });

// Receive decoded remote s16le PCM frames (e.g. feed into STT / Gemini Live):
const off = await tg.onAudioFrame(group, (frame) => {
  // frame: { ssrc, pcm: Buffer, timestampMs: bigint, peer? }
  stt.write(frame.pcm);
});

// Push synthesized s16le PCM audio back into the call (auto-sliced into 10ms frames):
await tg.pushAudioFrame(group, ttsPcmBuffer, { sampleRate: 48000, channels: 1 });
```

`{ kind: 'external' }` configures `MediaSource.EXTERNAL` with zero `ffmpeg` requirement and works in group calls, P2P calls (`listenCalls({ source: { kind: 'external' } })`), and conferences. `pushVideoFrame(chat, i420, { width, height })` pushes raw planar YUV420p frames to `camera` or `screen`. Both push helpers handle the `ntgcalls` JS-array N-API boundary automatically.

## Playback controls (`seek`, `setVolume`, `setSpeed`, `setLoop`)

```ts
await tg.play(group, { kind: 'file', path: './song.mp3' });
await tg.seek(group, 45);        // restart ffmpeg at -ss 45
await tg.setVolume(group, 150);  // 0..200% (-af volume=1.5)
await tg.setSpeed(group, 1.25);  // 0.5..2.0x (-af atempo=1.25, video setpts)
await tg.setLoop(group, 'all');  // 'off' | 'one' | 'all'
const controls = tg.getPlaybackControls(group); // { volume, speed, loop }
```

## Voice chat participant controls & `joinAs`

```ts
await tg.join(group, { kind: 'file', path: './song.mp3' }, { joinAs: '@mychannel' });
const peers = await tg.getParticipants(group);
await tg.setRaiseHand(group, true);
await tg.muteParticipant(group, userId, true);         // requires admin rights
await tg.setParticipantVolume(group, userId, 150);     // 0..200% (Telegram 0..20000)
```


<!-- ===== docs/ROADMAP.md ===== -->

# Call roadmap implementation

This working branch contains implementations for the roadmap in [#25](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/issues/25). New APIs below are **unreleased**. The last approved release remains `v0.8.0`; its tag does not contain these additions. No full parity claim is made for MadelineProto.

| Issue | Implemented behavior | Evidence and remaining acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [#17](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/issues/17) | `canRequestCall` / `getCallDenialReason`, profile flags and session checks without ringing | Concrete adapter fixtures and no-ringing regression pass; live read-only profile comparison remains open |
| [#19](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/issues/19) | Per-call outgoing recording override, inherited listener default, `false` to disable, active path collision checks | Outgoing fixture media, lifecycle and RPC-shape tests; finalization integration and candidate live recording still require final verification |
| [#18](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/issues/18) | Folder output by peer/device, MTProto participant registry, camera/screen subscriptions, segmented WAV/MP4 and manifest | Real PCM/I420 fixture output and public facade tests pass; two live publishers and real AV sync remain open |
| [#23](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/issues/23) | Unwrap `confirmCall`, preserve endpoints/protocol/custom JSON, direct P2P only with explicit permission | Red/green teleproto/mtcute-shaped regressions pass; candidate live adapter check remains open |
| [#20](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/issues/20) | RTMP H.264/AAC publisher plus separate server-selected stream viewer | Real RTMP loopback and controller/facade fixtures pass; actual Telegram key, viewer download/decode and reconnect remain open |
| [#21](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/issues/21) | Experimental native conference core, chain relay, invite, participant mappings, capability refusals | Offline port and labelled native simulator tests; full E2E/security acceptance blocked by native 3.0.7, live two-account test not run |
| [#22](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/issues/22) | Opt-in private atomic state file, explicit fresh group rejoin, queue/hold and new recording segments | Two-process persistence fixtures and facade restore pass; live restart acceptance remains open |
| [#24](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/issues/24) | Documented ffmpeg requirement and typed executable errors | MP4/WebM/MKV decode probes plus native FILE/FFMPEG investigation; combined candidate suite is the final gate |

No issue is closed solely because an offline suite passes. The independent review, final combined suite and GitHub CI status must be recorded separately in the delivery report.

## Corrections to the original diagnosis

`phone.confirmCall` returns a `phone.PhoneCall` wrapper containing `phoneCall` and `users`. The old outgoing path read the wrapper as the inner call, losing endpoints and permissions. `phone.getCall` is absent from both installed client schemas and the official MTProto schema. A slow answer was not established as the cause of the endpoint bug.

Outgoing calls already shared the listener recording setup through `startTransport`; the missing part was an explicit per-call API and reliable isolation/finalization. Native group source-change callbacks do not discover participants in the inspected binary: the new registry uses MTProto participant updates.

`sendBroadcastPart` supplies downloaded media to a native decoder. RTMP publication uses its own ffmpeg process and never uploads with that native method.

## Native and media limits

The pinned dependency is `ntgcalls@3.0.7`. Native FILE consumes raw PCM/I420; FFMPEG throws an unimplemented-encoder error. File/URL container playback requires ffmpeg. Caller-owned shell PCM does not require ffmpeg if it uses another producer. See [media support](media-support.md) for the source pins and measured decoder outputs.

Conference removal/rekey, encrypted application messages and observable cryptographic chain health are not exposed by native 3.0.7. These operations reject explicitly; there is no plaintext or custom JavaScript crypto replacement. A resolved `applyBlocks` promise and an emoji callback do not attest cryptographic conformance. The conference API is experimental until the native security and live gates are met.

State persistence stores group intent only. It does not serialize native sockets, SSRCs, P2P sessions, conference keys or RTMP keys. Restore starts the current source again and opens a fresh recording segment; it does not resume a native transport or provide gapless seeking.

## Verification contract

Run `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck:all`, `npm test`, and `npm run smoke` in a pinned cloud candidate. The canonical test runner discovers every `test/*.ts` entrypoint and isolates each in a fresh Node process. Media child processes must complete before native workers are created in tests that use both.

Live tests need an authorized user session and the requested peers/groups. Existing release-level live observations do not verify the changed candidate. Keep live requirements open until that candidate is exercised.


<!-- ===== docs/media-support.md ===== -->

# Media support and native decoder limits

For roadmap [#24](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/issues/24), the supported resolution is the **ffmpeg requirement fallback**. Install `ffmpeg` for container/file/URL audio and video sources and recording/muxing; install `ffprobe` for video metadata and sizing. The `ffmpegPath` and `ffprobePath` options select the executables. Supported container/codec combinations depend on the installed ffmpeg build.

There is no verified ffmpeg-free MP4, WebM or MKV decoder exposed by ntgcalls 3.0.7. This document makes no zero-transcode or compressed-packet passthrough claim. The wrapper decodes media to raw PCM/I420; native WebRTC subsequently handles its transport and encoding.

## What the source types mean

| API/source | Actual behavior | Requirement/limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wrapper `{ kind: 'file', path }` | `audioDescription` / `videoDescription` build native **SHELL** commands that run ffmpeg | A container readable by the installed ffmpeg build, with the requested audio/video stream |
| Wrapper `{ kind: 'url', url }` | ffmpeg opens the URL and produces raw frames; separate `audioUrl` is used for audio when present | Same decoder requirement plus network access |
| Wrapper `{ kind: 'shell', command }` | Caller-owned command produces raw audio | Caller must output 48 kHz stereo signed 16-bit little-endian PCM; this command need not use ffmpeg |
| Native `MediaSource.FILE` | Opens a binary file and reads raw frame-sized chunks | Headerless PCM for audio or planar I420 video matching the description; **no container demux or codec decode** |
| Native `MediaSource.FFMPEG` | Throws `FFmpeg encoder is not yet supported` | Unimplemented for input and audio output in the pinned source/runtime |
| Native `MediaSource.EXTERNAL` | Application supplies raw frames | Requires a real application decoder for compressed inputs; compressed packets are not raw frames |

`MediaSource.FILE` is the native enum, not the wrapper's `kind: 'file'`. Passing an MP4 path to native FILE and observing a resolved `setStreamSources()` promise proves only that the configuration/file was accepted. It does not show that frames were read, decoded, delivered or heard. In the probe below even a JSON file was accepted by FILE as an audio source.

No public `kind: 'media'` or generic native container source is introduced by this fallback. Example using the existing wrapper API:

```ts
await tg.join(group, { kind: 'file', path: './clip.mp4' }, {
  video: { width: 640, height: 360, fps: 25 },
  autoLeave: false,
});
// ffmpeg -> s16le stereo PCM + yuv420p/I420 -> native WebRTC
```

## Pinned source evidence

Wrapper baseline: [`bdb4582dc433a37f54681e9ce93581eac7c389d8`](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/tree/bdb4582dc433a37f54681e9ce93581eac7c389d8). Native dependency: **ntgcalls 3.0.7**; inspected upstream revision: [`6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557`](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls/tree/6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557). These are source/version pins; the installed prebuilt is identified separately by its hash below, not claimed to be a locally reproduced source build.

- [`src/media.ts` audio L10–31](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/blob/bdb4582dc433a37f54681e9ce93581eac7c389d8/src/media.ts#L10-L31) and [video L160–183](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/blob/bdb4582dc433a37f54681e9ce93581eac7c389d8/src/media.ts#L160-L183): file/URL inputs invoke ffmpeg and return `MediaSource.SHELL`. Audio is `-f s16le -ac 2 -ar 48000`; video is `-f rawvideo -pix_fmt yuv420p` with scaling and an explicit frame rate.
- [`MediaSourceFactory::from_input` L19–54](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls/blob/6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557/ntgcalls/src/media/media_source_factory.cpp#L19-L54): FILE constructs `io::FileReader`; FFMPEG throws at L43–45. [`from_audio_output` L57–78](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls/blob/6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557/ntgcalls/src/media/media_source_factory.cpp#L57-L78) throws the same exception for FFMPEG audio output at L72–74.
- [`FileReader` L9–45](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls/blob/6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557/ntgcalls/src/io/file_reader.cpp#L9-L45): binary `ifstream`, seek and `read(size)`; no media inspection, demuxer or codec decoder. [`ThreadedReader` L27–87](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls/blob/6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557/ntgcalls/src/io/threaded_reader.cpp#L27-L87) requests batches based on `sink_->frame_size()` and splits those bytes into frames.
- [`AudioSink` L9–19](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls/blob/6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557/ntgcalls/src/media/audio_sink.cpp#L9-L19): 10 ms frames, `sample_rate * 16 / 8 / 100 * channel_count` bytes. [`AudioStreamer` L20–26](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls/blob/6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557/ntgcalls/src/media/audio_streamer.cpp#L20-L26) sends these as 16-bit samples. The tested description uses 48 kHz stereo: 1,920 bytes per 10 ms.
- [`VideoSink` L11–22](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls/blob/6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557/ntgcalls/src/media/video_sink.cpp#L11-L22): `width * height * 1.5` bytes per frame. [`VideoStreamer` L20–39](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls/blob/6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557/ntgcalls/src/media/video_streamer.cpp#L20-L39) wraps those bytes as `I420ImageData`. Use even dimensions and matching frame rate. The fixture is 160×90 at 10 fps: 21,600 bytes per frame.
- [`StreamManager` L206–213](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls/blob/6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557/ntgcalls/src/media/stream_manager.cpp#L206-L213) opens configured readers when streams start; [`handle_capture_config` L489–519](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls/blob/6cbf3c5404e00f72dcefb85c6b8fb856f7078557/ntgcalls/src/media/stream_manager.cpp#L489-L519) only opens immediately when initialized. An offline configuration acceptance is not an observed playback pass.

## Observed cloud evidence

Probe date: **2026-11-21 UTC**. Target: InstaBox `m_agq62wtsnkqjj3hlchtinfk5fi` (`tgcalls-test`), cwd `/data/home/tgcalls-media-lane-20261121`. Environment: Linux x64, Node **v22.23.3**, npm **10.9.9**, ffmpeg/ffprobe **6.1.1-3ubuntu5**. The lane clones the pinned wrapper baseline; its `node_modules` points to `/data/home/tgcalls-inspection-20261121/node_modules`, used without installation or dependency changes.

Installed native binary `@ntgcalls/linux-x64/ntgcalls.node`: **100896624 bytes**, SHA-256 `0c62cbcc0dd321719738a0678bb207f21b0743d5a0c6a8335c0a5806b44bf7f8`. Native `NTgCalls.ping()` returned `pong`. Observed runtime enums are FILE=1, SHELL=2, FFMPEG=4, EXTERNAL=32; the test imports the enums instead of inferring values from ordinal declarations.

### Native probe

A separate initial `node evidence/native-probe.mjs` run exited **0** with empty stderr:

```text
FFMPEG microphone CAPTURE -> Error: FFmpeg encoder is not yet supported
FILE microphone with headerless s16le fixture -> configuration resolved
FILE microphone with package.json -> configuration resolved (counterexample only)
```

The more complete media probe also observed:

```text
FILE microphone s16le stereo 48000Hz + camera I420 160x90@10 -> configuration resolved
FFMPEG microphone CAPTURE -> FFmpeg encoder is not yet supported
FFMPEG microphone PLAYBACK -> FFmpeg encoder is not yet supported
FFMPEG camera CAPTURE -> FFmpeg encoder is not yet supported
FILE microphone with compressed MP4 -> configuration resolved (NOT decode evidence)
```

These are real native calls on fresh offline P2P placeholders, each stopped afterward. There was no Telegram transport or receiving peer, so native raw playback and delivered remote frames remain unobserved.

### Representative container decode

The test generates one-second synthetic audio/video using real ffmpeg, verifies encoded codecs with ffprobe, runs the **actual wrapper audio/video command strings**, and checks non-silent signed PCM plus detailed, complete I420 frames. All subprocesses finish before constructing `NTgCalls`. This is decoder/output evidence, not a live-call test.

| Container | ffprobe-confirmed encoded codecs | Decoded PCM bytes, 48 kHz stereo s16le | Peak absolute PCM sample | Decoded I420 bytes | Frames, 160×90 at 10 fps |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MP4 | H.264 + AAC | 192512 | 2979 | 216000 | 10 |
| WebM | VP9 + Opus | 192000 | 2931 | 216000 | 10 |
| MKV | HEVC/H.265 + AAC | 196608 | 2979 | 216000 | 10 |

AAC padding/timestamps make decoded audio lengths differ; the assertions allow approximately one second and check sample alignment. A deliberately corrupt MP4 produced **exit 183**, **0 decoded bytes** with the tested ffmpeg build. The assertion requires nonzero status rather than pinning a platform-specific exit number. The research probe exited **0** with empty stderr; its missing-dependency regression was explicitly excluded and reported separately as failing, so this result is **not** a full test pass.

These outputs were also reproduced by the complete `test/media-support.ts` after it was changed to retain a dependency-guard failure until all independent media probes finish. That complete run exited **1**, never emitted `MEDIA SUPPORT PASS`, and is retained as `verify-media-support.json` / `verification.json`.

The exercised encoder choices were `libx264`, `libvpx-vp9`, `libx265`, `aac`, `libopus`. This matrix is representative, not a guarantee for every codec profile, container combination, platform, ffmpeg build or URL. Upgrade the fixtures/source investigation when changing the native dependency.

### Missing-executable regression and integration requirement

Run the complete regression separately from `npm test`:

```sh
node --import tsx test/media-support.ts
```

The baseline `package.json` only runs `test/run.ts`; adding this file alone does not put it in that command. `npm run typecheck:all` does include it and exited **0** in the cloud lane. The first complete regression run against the pinned baseline exited **1**:

```text
AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Missing expected exception.
  at missingDependencies (.../test/media-support.ts:55:10)
```

This exposes a missing production guard, not an exempt pre-existing suite failure. The baseline receipt lists **no failing assertion exemption**. The complete regression retains a guard failure while continuing independent media evidence checks, then fails at the end; a research-only probe cannot close this regression.

Required guard behavior before passing a description to native:

- File/URL audio and video descriptions must reject a missing/non-executable `ffmpegPath` (default `ffmpeg`) with a `TgCallsError` subtype; the message identifies the executable and the `ffmpegPath` remedy. Recording commands require the same check.
- Video probing must reject a missing/non-executable `ffprobePath` with a typed error naming `ffprobePath`, rather than silently substituting default dimensions for ENOENT.
- Caller-owned shell/raw sources remain usable without ffmpeg. Resolving an executable should check PATH/file executability without spawning a child after native workers exist; this avoids introducing the known native-thread/process-spawn deadlock into every source helper.

The roadmap branch now implements these guards as `MediaDependencyError` and the complete media regression was rerun in the parent cloud worktree: `node --import tsx test/media-support.ts && npm run build && npm run typecheck:all` returned exit 0 (`media-support-green.json`). Executable discovery checks PATH and file executability without spawning. The research-phase red evidence above is retained as the regression witness. The canonical runner now discovers this entrypoint; the final combined candidate suite is still a separate gate.

One full verification pass on the isolated pinned baseline plus this lane's two artifacts returned:

| Check | Actual exit code | Scope/result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `npm run build` | 0 | Pinned wrapper source builds |
| `npm run typecheck:all` | 0 | Includes the new media-support test |
| `npm test` | 0 | Existing `test/run.ts`, `ALL TESTS PASSED`; intentional event-handler `Error: boom` fixture appears on stderr |
| `npm run smoke` | 0 | Built exports verified |
| `node --import tsx test/media-support.ts` | 1 | Container/native probes completed, missing executable guard still fails |
| `git diff --check` | 0 | Tracked patch whitespace check; the lane artifacts were new/untracked |

The overall verification command returned **1**. None of these results verifies the concurrent production changes in other lanes, a combined all-green candidate, Node 20, CI, live media, or a release.

### Reproducibility and receipts

Raw REST result envelopes and fetched pinned sources are retained locally in `/home/ocan/.hermes/cache/scratch/tgcalls-media-lane-20261121/`; cloud receipts are under `/data/home/tgcalls-media-lane-20261121/evidence/`. `evidence.json` records commands/results, pins, runtime/binary details and SHA-256 source receipts. `baseline-with-guard-test.json` preserves the original failing guard run, `research-probe.json` preserves the explicitly limited research-only run, and `source-manifest.json` pins the fetched source bytes. Generated fixtures are removed by the regression after inspection; measured output and hashes stay in the receipts.

To repeat: use the pinned dependencies, install an ffmpeg build with the listed codecs, then run the command above and `npm run typecheck:all`. Do not import this standalone test into a process that already owns native workers: it creates child processes, has a bounded deadline, and exits after stopping its own calls. A pass still requires separate authorized live playback/send/receive testing before claiming remote media support.


<!-- ===== docs/troubleshooting.md ===== -->

# Troubleshooting

## `Error: ntgcalls: no prebuilt binary for linux-x64`

Some npm versions (seen with **npm 12 installing from a git URL**) skip `ntgcalls`'
platform-specific optional dependency. Install it yourself, matching the `ntgcalls`
version in `package.json` (currently `3.0.7`):

```bash
npm install @ntgcalls/linux-x64@3.0.7 --no-save
```

Use the matching package on other platforms:

| Platform | Package |
|---|---|
| Linux x64 | `@ntgcalls/linux-x64` |
| Linux arm64 | `@ntgcalls/linux-arm64` |
| macOS arm64 | `@ntgcalls/darwin-arm64` |
| Windows x64 | `@ntgcalls/win32-x64` |

Installing from the npm registry (once published) resolves optional dependencies
normally and avoids this entirely. npm 10 (e.g. on many cloud images) installs the
binary correctly from a git URL.

## `default_launcher: No such file or directory (vfork_launcher)`

This confusing error from the native core almost always means **ffmpeg is not on
PATH**. ntgcalls spawns ffmpeg per source; without it you get a boost process-launch
ENOENT instead of a clear "ffmpeg not found".

```bash
sudo apt-get install ffmpeg     # Debian/Ubuntu
brew install ffmpeg             # macOS
ffmpeg -version                 # verify it resolves
```

The test suite now fails fast with a clear message if ffmpeg is missing.

## Join fails / kicked after ~25 seconds

On **UDP-blocked hosts** (some VPS/firewalls), a regular RTC join gets an ICE timeout
and Telegram kicks the participant after ~25s. Options:

- Use `joinIdle(chat, { allowCreate: true })` — creates the call in **RTMP-stream**
  mode and joins muted (no local media path needed). Existing calls are not converted.
- Presentation/screen share requires RTC and is **unavailable** in RTMP/STREAM mode.
- On UDP-capable hosts (verified on InstaBox/AWS), normal RTC joins and idle presence
  are stable indefinitely (40+ minutes tested).

Check outbound UDP:

```bash
timeout 5 bash -c 'exec 3<>/dev/udp/stun.l.google.com/19302' && echo "UDP OK"
```

## `NoVoiceChatError`

There is no active voice chat in the target chat. Start one manually, or pass
`allowCreate: true` (the account needs admin rights to create a call).

## `AlreadyInCallError`

You called `join`/`joinIdle` while already in a call (or mid-join) in that chat.
`leave(chat)` first. The error carries `chatId`.

## YouTube: "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot"

YouTube blocks **datacenter IPs** (cloud VMs) across all player clients. Fixes:

- **Cookies** from a logged-in browser (Netscape format):
  ```bash
  yt-dlp --cookies cookies.txt --js-runtimes node -f "bestvideo[vcodec~='^(vp09|avc1)']+bestaudio[ext=m4a]/best" URL
  ```
  Treat cookies as account credentials: store `chmod 600`, never log them, delete/rotate after use.
- A recent **yt-dlp** and a JS runtime (`--js-runtimes node` or deno) — extraction
  without a JS runtime is deprecated and may miss formats.
- Prefer `vp9`/`avc1` over AV1 for video (AV1 is too heavy to decode in real time on small VPS).
- Fallback: download from a residential IP, then transfer the file to the cloud host.

## Login / 2FA (teleproto)

- `client.start()` probes `updates.getState()`, which throws `AUTH_KEY_UNREGISTERED`
  on an empty session. For QR login use `client.signInUserWithQrCode(...)` directly;
  the QR token is a Buffer — encode `tg://login?token=<base64url>` for the QR image.
- For phone login, provide `phoneNumber`, `phoneCode`, and `password` (2FA) callbacks.
- Keep the resulting StringSession secret; reuse it with `new StringSession(str)` +
  `client.connect()`.

## Process aborts on exit

`process.exit()` immediately after native use can abort during WebRTC teardown
(cosmetic). `await tg.dispose()` and let queued callbacks drain before exiting;
long-running bots are unaffected.

## Mixing `telegram` and `teleproto`

Pass the matching `Api` namespace to each `TgCallsClient` to avoid ambiguous TL
auto-detection. mtcute uses its own TL schema and needs no `Api`.

## Incoming P2P call never connects (ICE `TIMEOUT`)

Four distinct failures can each stop a 1-on-1 call; the wrapper fixes them, but
they matter if you call `ntgcalls` directly or debug a fork:

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `An array was expected` from `initExchange` | `bytes::binary` is read as `Napi::Array` — `Buffer`/`Uint8Array` are rejected | pass `Array.from(buf)` |
| `phone.acceptCall` → `CALL_PEER_INVALID` | TL `long` is a `big-integer` object; `BigInt(obj)` goes through `Number` and loses precision | convert via `toString()` |
| `connectP2p` → `incomplete JSON [boost.json:3]` | `customParameters: ''` is a *present* optional; `json::parse("")` throws | pass `'{}'` |
| `Failed to parse received SCTP packet`, `Sorting 0 available connections`, then `TIMEOUT` | versions list includes `12.0.0`/`13.0.0` → ntgcalls routes signaling over an SCTP data channel, but Telegram sends it via MTProto | restrict to `8.0.0`/`9.0.0` |

Debug with `setLogLevel(LogLevel.DEBUG)` (from `ntgcalls`) and
`listenCalls({ debug: true })`. A healthy call logs, in order:
`Using signaling V2 Legacy` → `Decrypting packets` (inbound signaling) →
`new remote candidate` → `state= 2` (`CONNECTED`) →
`First audio RTP packet sent to pacer`.

## mtcute: no `INCOMING`, calls do nothing

Two mtcute-specific traps. Both are silent — no error is thrown.

1. **`client.connect()` does not start the updates loop.** `onRawUpdate` is
   emitted from that loop, so with `connect()` only outgoing RPCs work; no
   `updatePhoneCall` ever reaches the library. Use `client.start()` (it connects
   *and* launches the loop). Symptom: the call rings on the phone, the listener
   logs nothing at all.
2. **mtcute objects use `_`, GramJS/teleproto use `className`.** Fixed in the
   library (`kind` is normalised from either), but any custom adapter must do the
   same: `phoneCallRequested` vs `PhoneCallRequested`.

Verify the loop independently of calls:

```ts
client.onRawUpdate.add((u) => console.log('RAW', (u?.update ?? u)?._));
await client.sendText('me', 'self-test'); // must log RAW updateMessageID
```

Session note: a GramJS/teleproto string session can be reused with mtcute via
`@mtcute/convert` (`convertFromGramjsSession`) + `client.importSession()`.

## Outgoing call: ICE `TIMEOUT` (state 8) right after the peer answers

`phone.confirmCall` returns a wrapper `{phoneCall, users}`. Reading `connections` from the wrapper instead of `phoneCall` loses the server list and peer permission flags. The roadmap branch unwraps this response and passes the inner endpoints, protocol and custom JSON to native. Direct P2P is allowed only when `p2pAllowed === true`.

`phone.getCall` is absent from both installed client schemas and the official MTProto schema. It is not a fallback for this shape error. There is no established evidence that slow answering caused the missing endpoints. If a current call still fails, inspect the confirmed inner call and fresh native/signaling logs rather than adding a nonexistent RPC.


<!-- ===== AGENTS.md ===== -->

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for coding agents working on **tgcalls-js**.

## What this is

A TypeScript wrapper (`src/`) around the `ntgcalls` native binding that streams
audio/video into Telegram voice chats via a GramJS-family or mtcute MTProto client.
ESM (`"type": "module"`), strict TypeScript, Node ≥ 18.

## Commands

```bash
npm install            # npm 11+ may warn "install scripts blocked" for esbuild — cosmetic
npm run build          # tsc → dist/
npm run typecheck:all  # tsc -p tsconfig.all.json (src + examples + test)
npm test               # node test/all.mjs — every test/*.ts in isolated processes, NO credentials
npm run smoke          # node smoke.mjs — verify dist/index.js exports
```

CI without GitHub Actions: `scripts/ci.sh` (npm ci → build → typecheck:all → test →
smoke; `--fresh [ref]` clones pristine first). GitHub Actions may be disabled at the
account level — prefer `scripts/ci.sh` for verification.

## Hard rules

- **Never run live joins without an explicit user-account session and permission.**
  Bots cannot join voice chats. The offline test suite is the default verification path.
- The offline suite uses a **fake MTProto client + the real ntgcalls native core** — it
  proves protocol plumbing (ssrc round-trip, cleanup, races, dispose) without login.
- `ffmpeg` must be on PATH to run `npm test`; the suite fails fast with a clear message
  if it is missing.

## Native binary pitfall

`npm install` from a git URL on some npm versions (e.g. npm 12) skips the optional
`@ntgcalls/linux-x64` package → `Error: ntgcalls: no prebuilt binary for linux-x64`.
Fix: `npm install @ntgcalls/linux-x64@3.0.7 --no-save` (match the `ntgcalls` version).

## Domain pitfalls (do not regress these)

- Join order is fixed: getFullChannel → createCall → setStreamSources → joinGroupCall
  → connect. The same join-params string goes to JoinGroupCall; its ssrc is reused for
  LeaveGroupCall.
- `setStreamSources` REPLACES all devices — omitting the video channel drops it.
  `setSource()` must rebuild video. Camera and screen cannot be active simultaneously.
- `streamEnd` fires once per playback; with video, wait for BOTH audio and video to end
  before auto-leave.
- A failed join must stop the native call and send LeaveGroupCall (no zombie participant).
- mtcute TL `Long` (low/high) objects must be preserved by reference — do not convert to
  bigint. GramJS/teleproto use plain bigint.
- `ConnectionState` is numeric (CONNECTING=1, CONNECTED=2, FAILED=4, TIMEOUT=8, CLOSED=16).
- On native CLOSED/FAILED, leave via MTProto BEFORE notifying listeners.

## Conventions

- Library errors extend `TgCallsError` (`src/errors.ts`); add new typed errors there.
- Internal warnings go through `opts.logger` (default `console.error`) — do not
  `console.log` directly from library code.
- Public API is re-exported from `src/index.ts`; keep `src/types.ts` the source of truth
  for shared types. Examples live in `examples/`, tests in `test/`.
- Examples use `teleproto` (the maintained GramJS fork); runtime still supports `telegram`.
- Docs: `README.md`, `docs/*.md`, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`. Keep them in sync with the
  public API when you change signatures. `llms-full.txt` is generated from the
  sources declared in `scripts/generate-docs.py`: run `python3 scripts/generate-docs.py`
  and verify with `python3 scripts/generate-docs.py --check`.

## Release

Version in `package.json` + a `CHANGELOG.md` entry. Tag `vX.Y.Z` and
`gh release create vX.Y.Z` (releases via gh API work even when Actions is disabled).


<!-- ===== CHANGELOG.md ===== -->

# Changelog

## 0.9.0 (2026-11-23)

- **Call preflight without ringing (#17):** `canRequestCall()` and `getCallDenialReason()` via `users.getFullUser` and session checks on both GramJS/teleproto and mtcute adapters (verified live).
- **Outgoing P2P recording & finalization (#19):** per-call `OutgoingCallOptions.record` override (`false` to disable, string/object to override listener default), active path collision guards, `.webm` rejection for H.264/AAC muxing, recovery file retention on failure, setup-error cleanup, and `recordingStopped` / `recordingError` events (verified live: `1280×720` H.264/AAC MP4).
- **Outgoing `confirmCall` unwrap & RTC servers (#23):** unwraps `phone.PhoneCall { phoneCall, users }`, removes nonexistent `phone.getCall`, preserves relay endpoints, protocol versions, `customParameters`, and explicit `p2pAllowed` (verified live: `servers=2`, `CONNECTED`).
- **RTMP publisher & broadcast stream viewer (#20):** `getStreamRtmpUrl()` (`revoke: false`), `joinRtmp()` (`RtmpPublisher`), and `joinStreamMode()` (`BroadcastController`) with explicit media-DC routing (verified live on Telegram RTMP ingest & DC 5).
- **Per-participant folder recording (#18):** `startRecording(chat, { dir, video })`, `ParticipantRegistry`, `GroupParticipantController`, `FolderRecorder`, MTProto participant pagination/delta/min-field merge cache, attributed `remoteSourceChange` (`origin: 'mtproto'`), and `manifest.json` (verified live for single remote participant + multi-peer offline).
- **Opt-in state persistence & fresh resume (#22):** `statePath`, `flushState()`, and `resumeFromState()` with atomic writes, fresh group rejoin/SSRC allocation, playlist restore, and fresh recording segment directories (verified live).
- **Experimental native conference core (#21):** `createConference()`, `joinConference()`, `exportConferenceInvite()`, `inviteConferenceParticipants()`, `getEmojiFingerprint()`, and `leaveConference()` (2-account live E2E audio + matching 4-emoji fingerprint verified; removal/rekey and encrypted app messages remain blocked by `ntgcalls@3.0.7`).
- **Media requirements (#24):** documented `ntgcalls@3.0.7` `FILE`/`FFMPEG` limits and `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` requirements in `docs/media-support.md`; added `MediaDependencyError`.
- **Isolated test runner:** `npm test` (`test/all.mjs`) runs every `test/*.ts` entrypoint in an isolated Node process (`18/18` passing).

## 0.8.0 (2026-11-20)

- Feat: **P2P calls on mtcute** — the adapter now implements accept/request/
  confirm/signaling/discard and routes `updatePhoneCall` + `updatePhoneCallSignalingData`.
  Two silent traps fixed: `client.connect()` never starts mtcute's updates loop
  (use `start()`), and phone-call updates carry `_` (`phoneCallRequested`) while the
  dispatcher only read `className`.
- Feat: **video in outgoing calls** — `callUser(userId, { video })` mounts the camera
  device and asks Telegram for a video call; verified live (ICE `CONNECTED`,
  `Encoder is active`, audio RTP flowing).
- Fix: `phone.requestCall` result is wrapped (`{ phoneCall, users }`) — the call id
  was read from the wrapper and came out as `0`.
- Fix: `phone.confirmCall` has no `gB` field; the adapter now sends `gA` and a raw
  `Buffer` (the native-facing `jsBytes()` array is wrong for MTProto).

## 0.7.1 (2026-11-20)

- Fix: **`connectionChange` now reports the final state** — after a peer hangs up
  (or `stopListeningCalls()` runs) consumers received no transition, so state maps
  stayed stuck on `CONNECTED` (2). `P2PCallManager` emits `ConnectionState.CLOSED`
  (16) for each torn-down peer. Covered by an offline test.
## 0.7.0 (2026-11-20)

**P2P calls now work end-to-end — verified live** (ICE `CONNECTED`, audio RTP flowing,
caller hears the stream). Four defects were fixed on the way; all were silent or
misattributed, so they are documented here.

- Fix: **byte parameters must be JS arrays** — the ntgcalls N-API glue reads
  `bytes::binary` via `v.As<Napi::Array>()`, so `Buffer`/`Uint8Array`/`ArrayBuffer`
  throw `An array was expected`. New `jsBytes()` helper converts at every binding
  boundary (`initExchange` p/random/gaHash, `exchangeKeys` gAOrB, `sendSignalingData`,
  `RTCServer.peerTag`). The published `index.d.ts` claiming `Buffer` is wrong.
- Fix: **64-bit TL integers were lossy** — teleproto represents `long` as a
  `big-integer` object; `BigInt(obj)` goes through `valueOf()` → `Number` and loses
  precision above 2^53, so `accessHash` was corrupted and `phone.acceptCall` returned
  `CALL_PEER_INVALID`. New `asBigInt0()` converts via `toString()`.
- Fix: **`connectP2p` customParameters** — `''` is a *present* optional, so the native
  `json::parse("")` threw `incomplete JSON`. Now sends `'{}'`.
- Fix: **signaling version selection** — ntgcalls picks the highest supported version
  from the list; `12.0.0`/`13.0.0` select `SignalingSctpConnection` (signaling over the
  SCTP data channel), but Telegram 1:1 calls carry signaling over MTProto. Inbound
  packets were fed into SCTP (`Failed to parse received SCTP packet`), remote candidates
  never reached ICE, and the call timed out with `Sorting 0 available connections`.
  Now restricted to the peer's V2 subset (`8.0.0`/`9.0.0`).
- Feat: `listenCalls({ debug: true })` for per-step signaling/ICE diagnostics; the
  verbose `[p2p]` logs are off by default.
- Docs: P2P marked verified; implementer notes on arrays, V2 signaling and `debug`.

## 0.6.0 (2026-11-19)

> **Superseded by 0.7.0** — the blocker described below was a binding-usage issue,
> not an upstream bug: byte arguments must be plain JS arrays. P2P works in 0.7.0.

> **⚠️ P2P calls are EXPERIMENTAL and not yet functional live.** The signaling
> orchestration is implemented and offline-tested, but actual calls are blocked by
> an ntgcalls **JS-binding** bug: `initExchange` throws `An array was expected`
> when converting `DhConfig` (`std::vector<byte>`) — reproduced with Buffer /
> Uint8Array / Array / ArrayBuffer / DataView inputs, on ntgcalls 3.0.7 **and**
> 3.1.0-beta01. The Python/Go bindings accept the same inputs. Needs an upstream
> ntgcalls fix before P2P works end-to-end. Group-call features are unaffected.

- Feat: **multi-handler events** — `on()` now supports multiple handlers per event
  (all run in registration order) and returns an unsubscribe function; new `off()`
  and `once()`. A throwing handler no longer blocks the others. Previously the last
  registration won. Non-breaking for single-handler use.
- Feat (experimental): **incoming P2P (1-on-1) voice calls** — `listenCalls({ source, autoAccept?, onIncoming? })`,
  `stopListeningCalls()`, `activeCallPeers()`. Answers incoming Telegram voice calls
  and streams an audio source into them. The DH key exchange and WebRTC engine run
  in the ntgcalls native core; the library orchestrates the MTProto signaling
  (`phone.acceptCall` / `sendSignalingData`, `UpdatePhoneCall` / `UpdatePhoneCallSignalingData`),
  including signaling queueing before connect and clean teardown on discard.
- Adapter: new optional P2P methods on `MTProtoAdapter` (getDhConfig/acceptCall/
  requestCall/confirmCall/discardCall/sendSignalingData/installCallHandler/resolveUserId),
  implemented for GramJS/teleproto. New `P2PCallManager` + `ListenCallsOptions` exports.
- Scope: incoming calls only this release; outgoing calls and multi-party conference
  are follow-up phases. Requires a GramJS/teleproto client (mtcute P2P not yet wired).
- Docs: P2P section in guide + API reference; `examples/call-gramjs.ts`.

## 0.5.0 (2026-11-19)

- Feat: call recording — `startRecording(chat, path, opts?)`, `stopRecording(chat)`,
  `getRecording(chat)`, `isRecording(chat)`. Records **incoming** call audio:
  ntgcalls mixes all remote speakers (its native `ThreadedAudioMixer`) and pipes
  s16le PCM to ffmpeg, which encodes to `path` (container from the extension:
  `.wav` / `.mp3` / `.opus`). Options: `sampleRate` (default 48000), `channels`
  (default 1). Stopping SIGTERMs ffmpeg so the container finalizes cleanly.
- New types: `RecordOptions`, `RecordingInfo`; new media helper `recordingDescription()`.
- Docs: recording section in the guide + API reference; `examples/record-gramjs.ts`.

## 0.4.0 (2026-11-19)

- Feat: built-in playlist/queue — `play()`, `enqueue()`/`then()`, `skip()`,
  `playOnHold()`, `clearQueue()`, `getCurrent()`, `getQueue()`. Tracks advance
  automatically when each one ends; a hold track loops while the queue is empty.
  The call only auto-leaves when the queue **and** hold are empty. `skip()` with
  nothing queued pauses playback (the call stays open).
- Non-breaking: the lower-level `setSource()`/`join()` and the manual `streamEnd`
  queue pattern still work unchanged.
- Docs: playlist section in the guide + API reference; new `examples/playlist-gramjs.ts`.

## 0.3.1 (2026-11-18)

- Fix: typed errors — new `TgCallsError` base plus `AlreadyInCallError`,
  `NoVoiceChatError`, `UnrecognizedClientError` (with `chatId` where
  applicable) replace bare `Error` throws, so consumers can `instanceof`
  instead of matching message strings. All still extend `Error`.
- Feat: `logger` option on `TgCallsOptions` — route the library's internal
  warnings (e.g. a throwing event handler) into your own logger. Defaults to
  `console.error` (previous behaviour).
- Fix: test suite now fails fast with a clear message when `ffmpeg` is not on
  PATH (previously the missing binary surfaced from ntgcalls as a confusing
  `vfork_launcher` ENOENT crash).
- Chore: dev dependency `telegram` (archived GramJS) replaced by its maintained
  fork `teleproto`; examples updated. Runtime support for `telegram` is
  unchanged.
- Docs: install troubleshooting for the native binary on npm versions that
  skip optional dependencies, and the ffmpeg PATH requirement.

## 0.3.0 (2026-11-10)

- Feat: Add support for mtcute (`@mtcute/node`, `@mtcute/core`) via modular `MTProtoAdapter` and automatic client detection.
- Feat: Export `MtcuteAdapter`, `GramjsAdapter`, `createAdapter`, `isMtcuteClient`, and `isGramjsClient`.

- Fix: `setSource()` no longer drops the camera/screen video channel (ntgcalls removes any device omitted from `setStreamSources`); the video is rebuilt from the new source.
- Fix: `streamEnd` fires once per playback. With video active it waits for both audio and video to end (was: once per stream type, auto-leaving early).
- Fix: a failed `join()` now stops the native call and sends `LeaveGroupCall` (no zombie participant).
- Fix: an event handler that throws/rejects no longer crashes the process (logged instead).
- Fix: `joinYouTube()` with video/presentation now requests separate `bestvideo[height<=720]+bestaudio` streams (new `resolveYouTubeStreams()`, `audioUrl` on url sources) instead of the low-res pre-merged format that looked blurry.
- Perf: video scaling `lanczos` -> `bicubic` (lighter on small VPS).
- `startPresentation()`: skips the empty idle audio source; marks camera inactive (ntgcalls can't mix camera and screen).

## 0.2.0 (2026-09-08)

- Video sharing: `join(..., { video: {width, height, fps} })`
- Screen share: `startPresentation()` / `stopPresentation()`
- `joinIdle()` for stable idle presence

## 0.1.0 (2026-09-08)

First release. Audio-only.

- `join()` / `joinYouTube()` with file / URL / shell PCM sources
- `setSource()` — swap track without leaving (queue support)
- `pause` / `resume` / `mute` / `unmute` / `leave` / `time`
- Events: `streamEnd`, `connectionChange`, `update`
- Works with GramJS (`telegram`) and teleproto; offline test suite with fake
  MTProto + real ntgcalls native core
